ns1:channel.ns1:title: Communications Earth & Environment
ns1:channel.ns1:description:
Communications Earth & Environment is an open access journal from Nature Portfolio that publishes high-quality research, reviews and commentary in the Earth, environmental and planetary sciences. The papers we publish represent significant advances that bring new insight to a specialized area of research. We also provide a community forum for issues of importance to Earth, environmental and planetary scientists, regardless of sub-discipline.

Our scope covers all areas of the geosciences, climate and environmental sciences as well as planetary sciences, including those at the interface with ecology, sustainability and environmental social sciences. Primary research of interest to the journal includes important insights gained from field work, novel analyses of existing data, numerical or analytical modelling, theoretical studies or laboratory experiments.

We encourage submissions that provide independent confirmation of particularly influential publications.

The submission and review processes are managed by our in-house professional editors supported by our Editorial Board Members, who provide technical expertise across the breadth of the Earth, environmental and planetary sciences. We are committed to rapid dissemination of important research results. Articles are published on a continuous basis to ensure swift communication of findings.

ns1:item.ns1:title: Fluid inclusions establish natron as a key astrobiological target on Enceladus
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 06 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04080-z

Natron precipitation traps and preserves pockets of parent fluid, providing a window into the geochemistry of Saturn’s moon Enceladus’ interior, establishing it as a mineral of high astrobiological importance, shown using freezing behaviour experiments and combined synchrotron X-ray computed microtomography and diffraction.
ns1:item.dc:title: Fluid inclusions establish natron as a key astrobiological target on Enceladus
ns1:item.dc:creator: Liam J. Perera
James Le Houx
Alberto Leonardi
Sarah J. Day
Stephen P. Thompson
ns1:item.dc:source: Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 2026-10-06; | doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04080-z

ns1:item.ns1:title: Carbon source and pollutant matching shapes microbial succession and removal regimes under electrochemical redox control
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 06 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04100-y

Decision-oriented carbon supplementation in electro-assisted and related anaerobic wastewater treatment systems reshapes niches and interspecies dependencies, leading to around 4-fold increase in pollutant removal, based on experiments pairing three carbon sources with three pollutants.

ns1:item.ns1:title: Marine arsenate evolution during Proterozoic oxygenation events and implications for biological phosphate metabolism
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 06 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-03976-0

Arsenate-to-phosphate ratios increased with the Great Oxygenation Event, potentially limiting productivity and oxygenation. Post-glaciation phosphorus enrichment during the Neoproterozoic Oxygenation Event reduced ratios toward modern levels, enhancing phosphate metabolism, oxygenation, marine productivity and supporting eukaryotic expansion.
ns1:item.dc:title: Marine arsenate evolution during Proterozoic oxygenation events and implications for biological phosphate metabolism
